prompt: A dashboard designed 960 pixels wide is shrunk to fit a 360-pixel phone. A label drawn at 10 pixels arrives at how many pixels?
What is a CSS pixel?

choices.text: One physical dot on the screen, whatever the phone
choices.why: Sharp screens use several dots per CSS pixel.

choices.text: A pixel of an image saved as PNG
choices.why: Image pixels are a different thing.

choices.text: The browser's unit of layout
choices.why: Right. A sharp phone screen packs two or three physical pixels into each.

choices.text: A unit used only in print stylesheets
choices.why: It is the screen's layout unit.

prompt: What is the difference between shrinking a dashboard and reflowing it?

choices.text: Shrinking is quicker for the phone's browser to draw
choices.why: Speed is not the difference that matters.

choices.text: Reflowing keeps the sizes and changes the layout
choices.why: Right. Shrinking does the opposite.

choices.text: Reflowing removes the charts and keeps the numbers
choices.why: Nothing has to be removed.

choices.text: They are two names for one technique
choices.why: They are opposites.

prompt: About how wide is a phone held upright, in CSS pixels?

choices.why: Those are physical pixels on many phones.
That is a laptop.
Too narrow even for a small phone.
Right.

prompt: In what order do a dashboard's blocks stack on a phone?

choices.text: Alphabetically by the title of each chart
choices.why: Alphabetical order says nothing about importance.

choices.text: In order of importance, most important first
choices.why: Right, the same order lesson 18 laid them out in.

choices.text: Smallest chart first, so the page starts fast
choices.why: Size of file is not size of importance.

choices.text: In whatever order the tool chooses
choices.why: The tool does not know what matters.

prompt: A detail table has six columns. What does the lesson suggest for the phone version?

choices.text: Cut it to the columns that matter, or replace or link it
choices.why: Right. Six columns do not fit 360 pixels at a readable size.

choices.text: Shrink the font until all six fit
choices.why: Then nobody can read it.

choices.text: Leave it and let the reader scroll sideways
choices.why: Sideways scrolling loses the row's start.

choices.text: Turn the column headings sideways
choices.why: That fixes the headings, not the width.

prompt: When may two cards share a row on a phone?

choices.text: When both numbers still fit at a readable size
choices.why: Right. Three cannot.

choices.text: Whenever the cards are the same colour
choices.why: Colour does not make room.

choices.text: Never: one card per row, always
choices.why: Two short cards can share.

choices.text: When the phone is held sideways
choices.why: Design for the phone held upright.

prompt: Why do horizontal bars suit a phone better than columns?

choices.text: Horizontal bars use noticeably less ink than columns do
choices.why: The ink is about the same.

choices.text: Phones cannot draw vertical shapes
choices.why: They can.

choices.text: Columns cannot start at zero on a phone
choices.why: They can; the labels are the problem.

choices.text: Width is scarce on a phone, while height is free
choices.why: Right. The labels get whole lines.

prompt: A time axis had five date labels on the laptop. Which ones does the lesson keep on the phone?

choices.text: All five, turned sideways to fit
choices.why: Sideways labels are read with a tilted head.

choices.text: Only the middle one, as a reference
choices.why: The middle does not frame the period.

choices.text: None of them: the line is enough
choices.why: Without dates the reader does not know the period.

choices.text: The first and the last
choices.why: Right. They frame the period.

prompt: On a phone, what replaces a legend beside the chart?

choices.text: Direct labels at the end of each line
choices.why: Right, lesson 15's labels.

choices.text: A legend below the chart, in smaller type
choices.why: Smaller type is harder to read on a phone.

choices.text: A tooltip that appears when a line is hovered
choices.why: There is no hover on a phone.

choices.text: Colours chosen to be self-explanatory
choices.why: No colour names itself.

prompt: On a narrow screen, width is scarce and ___ is free, because the page scrolls.
What target size does WCAG 2.2 ask for at level AA?

choices.text: At least 24 by 24 CSS pixels
choices.why: Right, or enough space around a smaller one.

choices.text: At least 16 by 16 CSS pixels
choices.why: That is the small arrow the lesson calls too small.

choices.text: At least 48 by 48 CSS pixels
choices.why: That is close to Material's recommendation.

choices.text: Any size, as long as it has a label
choices.why: A label does not make it easier to hit.

prompt: Match each guideline to the target size it asks for.
A chart shows each month's value only in a tooltip when hovered. What is the problem on a phone?

choices.text: Tooltips use too much of the phone's battery
choices.why: Battery is not the issue.

choices.text: Tooltips are too large for a narrow screen
choices.why: Their size is not the problem; reaching them is.

choices.text: Phones show tooltips in a different language
choices.why: Language has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A touch screen has no resting pointer
choices.why: Right. Anything needed must be visible without hovering.

prompt: How many CSS pixels wide is the smallest target WCAG 2.2 accepts at level AA, without extra spacing?
What does `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` do?

choices.text: Makes every image on the page twice as sharp
choices.why: It is about layout, not sharpness.

choices.text: Stops the reader from zooming into the whole page
choices.why: It does not block zoom, and nothing should.

choices.text: Turns on the browser's device mode
choices.why: Device mode is a developer tool.

choices.text: Lays the page out at the phone's real width
choices.why: Right. Without it the browser pretends to be about 980 pixels wide.

prompt: Where should a breakpoint go?

choices.text: At the exact width of the director's phone
choices.why: The next phone will be different.

choices.text: At 1,024 pixels, the common laptop width
choices.why: A fixed number ignores this layout.

choices.text: At half the width of the widest chart
choices.why: That is arithmetic, not a test of the layout.

choices.text: Wherever the layout itself stops working
choices.why: Right, not at a particular phone's width.

prompt: What does the `<picture>` element let the page do?

choices.text: Show a photograph behind the chart
choices.why: That would be chartjunk.

choices.text: Draw a chart without any SVG file
choices.why: It still needs the files.

choices.text: Offer two charts and a rule to choose between them
choices.why: Right: the narrow SVG at 600 pixels or less.

choices.text: Make the chart interactive
choices.why: It only chooses a file.

prompt: Why does the lesson bind the test server to 127.0.0.1 rather than 0.0.0.0 by default?

choices.text: Because 0.0.0.0 makes the server run slower
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: Because phones cannot open 0.0.0.0 addresses at all
choices.why: 0.0.0.0 is how a phone on the network reaches it.

choices.text: So the folder stays visible to this computer alone
choices.why: Right. 0.0.0.0 shows it to everyone on the network.

choices.text: Because 127.0.0.1 enables device mode
choices.why: Device mode is in the browser.
